block_instructions: Ask for approval before you run `git reset`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Every form moves HEAD and can orphan commits, eventually lost to GC.
Ask for approval before you run `git clean (-[A-Za-z]*f|--force)`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Deletes untracked files irrecoverably; only the force forms delete.

Ask for approval before you run `git branch( +[^ ]+)* +(-[A-Za-z]*[dDmMfC]|--(delete|move|force))`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Deletes, renames, force-moves or force-copies a branch, which throws away a ref the user made. Creating one is a git write too, which needs its own ask from the user.

Ask for approval before you run `git tag( +[^ ]+)* +(-[A-Za-z]*[df]|--(delete|force))`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Deletes or force-moves a tag, which throws away a ref the user made. Others can already have fetched that tag.

Ask for approval before you run `git checkout`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Changes the branch or checkout this session works in. Other agents work in this folder at the same time, so every agent and subagent stays on the branch and checkout the session started in, plans included, until the user asks for a change. Its `--` form also overwrites files with no reflog to recover them.

Ask for approval before you run `git (checkout-index|read-tree|sparse-checkout)`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Writes files into the checkout or the index, or changes which files the checkout has. No reflog keeps the old state.
Ask for approval before you run `git restore`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Always rewrites index or worktree; no variant is safe enough to allow.
Ask for approval before you run `git stash`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Moves uncommitted work somewhere the user did not put it.

Ask for approval before you run `git switch`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Changes the branch or checkout this session works in. Other agents work in this folder at the same time, so every agent and subagent stays on the branch and checkout the session started in, plans included, until the user asks for a change.

Ask for approval before you run `git bisect`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Changes the branch or checkout this session works in. Other agents work in this folder at the same time, so every agent and subagent stays on the branch and checkout the session started in, plans included, until the user asks for a change.
Ask for approval before you run `git rebase`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Rewrites history that may already be shared.

Ask for approval before you run `git filter-(branch|repo)`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Rewrites every commit in the history. Others can already have pulled those commits.

Ask for approval before you run `git pull( +[^ ]+)* +(-[A-Za-z]*r|--rebase)`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Rebases local commits onto the fetched branch, which rewrites them.

Ask for approval before you run `git( +[^ ]+)* +--abort$`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Stops a merge, cherry-pick, revert, am or rebase and puts the tree back to its state before the operation. Changes made since then can be lost.

Ask for approval before you run `git commit( +[^ ]+)* +--amend`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Rewrites the last commit, in any flag order; a plain commit stays allowed.
Ask for approval before you run `git rm`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Removes tracked files from the worktree, not just the index.
Ask for approval before you run `git gc`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Prunes unreachable objects that are the recovery path for a bad reset.
Ask for approval before you run `git prune`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Same recovery-path destruction as gc.
Ask for approval before you run `git reflog (expire|delete|drop)`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: The reflog is the last thing standing after a destructive command.
Ask for approval before you run `git update-ref`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Moves refs beneath the porcelain, bypassing every other guard.

Ask for approval before you run `git symbolic-ref( +[^ ]+)* +(-[A-Za-z]*d|--delete|[^ ]*HEAD +refs/)`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Points HEAD at another branch with no checkout, or deletes a symbolic ref. A read with one name, such as `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` or `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, stays allowed.

Ask for approval before you run `git worktree (add|move)`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Changes the branch or checkout this session works in. Other agents work in this folder at the same time, so every agent and subagent stays on the branch and checkout the session started in, plans included, until the user asks for a change.

Ask for approval before you run `git worktree (remove|prune)`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Deletes a checkout that may hold uncommitted work, or the admin data that finds one. Only `list` is a read; `add` and `move` are git writes, which need their own ask from the user.

Ask for approval before you run `git push( +[^ ]+)* +(-[A-Za-z]*[fd]|--(force|delete|mirror|prune)|\+|:)`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Force-pushes, or deletes or prunes refs on the remote, which others may already have pulled. A plain push, `-u`, `--follow-tags` and a `HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>` refspec stay allowed.

Ask for approval before you run `git fetch( +[^ ]+)* +(-[A-Za-z]*f|--force|\+)`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Force-updates local branches or tags, which can throw away commits. A `+` refspec, as in `origin +main:main`, also forces the update.

Ask for approval before you run `wt (switch|remove|merge|step|hook)`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Changes the branch or checkout this session works in. Other agents work in this folder at the same time, so every agent and subagent stays on the branch and checkout the session started in, plans included, until the user asks for a change. `wt list` is a read.

Ask for approval before you run `gh pr (checkout|co|merge)` or `gh repo sync`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Changes the branch or checkout this session works in. Other agents work in this folder at the same time, so every agent and subagent stays on the branch and checkout the session started in, plans included, until the user asks for a change.

Ask for approval before you run `gh pr close( +[^ ]+)* +(-d|--delete-branch)`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Deletes the local and remote branch of the pull request. Others can still need that branch.

Ask for approval before you run `gh repo (delete|archive|rename)`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Deletes, archives or renames a repository on GitHub, which changes it for every user.

Ask for approval before you run `gh release (delete|delete-asset)`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Deletes a release or its files on GitHub. Others can already use them.

Ask for approval before you run `gh api( +[^ ]+)* +(-X *|--method[ =])DELETE`, and run it only when the user asked for that action in the chat: Sends a DELETE request, which deletes data on GitHub, such as a branch, a tag or a release.
Each rule above also holds after a global option, as in `git -C <dir> reset`, `git -c <key>=<value> push --force` or `wt -C <path> switch`.

Agents read git. They run a git, gh or wt write only when the user asked for that action in the chat. One ask to commit or push covers a run of work; each other write needs its own ask. Never run a write to ask the user through its approval prompt.
